# Environment Setup

Download R and RStudio. Install the standard R libraries for package development by running the R code `install.packages(c("devtools", "usethis", "roxygen2", "testthat"))`. Windows users will also need to install Rtools (https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) and macOS users will need Xcode Command Line Tools (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/installing-the-command-line-tools). Follow the installation instructions on the above sites.

# Package Development

## Metadata

The DESCRIPTION file contains directly editable metadata, including title, description, and authors.

## Developing

To create a new R file in the package, run `usethis::use_r("my_function")` or manually add a `my_function.R` file to the `R/` folder. Use `roxygen2` inline comments to add documentation to exported functions:

```{r}
#' Add Two Numbers
#'
#' @description
#' Takes two numeric vectors and returns their element-wise sum.
#'
#' @param x A numeric vector or single number.
#' @param y A numeric vector or single number.
#' 
#' @return A numeric vector representing the sum of \code{x} and \code{y}.
#' 
#' @examples
#' # Add two single numbers
#' add_numbers(3, 5)
#' 
#' @export
add_numbers <- function(x, y) { ... }
```

To create the documentation files based on the `roxygen2` comments, run `devtools::document`. This updates files in the `man/` directory and updates the `NAMESPACE` file.

Vignettes are long-form tutorials in the documentation. To create a vignette, run `usethis::use_vignette("my-vignette")`. This created an editable `.Rmd` file in the `vignettes/` directory. Ensure the YAML `title` and `VignetteIndexEntry` match.

To update the public-facing documentation website, run `pkgdown::build_site()`. To view the website, open `index.html` in the `docs/` folder.

## Testing

To manually load and test package functions, you may run `devtools::load_all()` or `devtools::install()`. `devtools::load_all()` makes the package functions temporarily available in the current R session. `devtools::install()` adding the package to the computer's R package library and making it available to use in normal R sessions, similar to `install.packages()`.

To create an automatic test case, run TODO. To run the test suite, run `devtools::test()`.

## Publishing

First, perform diagnostic checks by running `devtools::check()`. Then, compile the package by running `devtools::build()`.
